newsitem.title: USA: IBM surges on Merrill, SoundView moves.
newsitem.headline: IBM surges on Merrill, SoundView moves.

text.p: Shares of International Business Machines Corp continued to surge after an influential Merrill Lynch analyst upgraded IBM and SoundView Financial issued a more upbeat view for technology stocks, traders said.

The stock also had a minor technical breakout, breaking through a minor consolidation level of 120, market technicians said. Technicians said the stock is now poised to reach another resistance level of around 129.
"People are starting to take another look at technology," one trader said. "And IBM is the number one tech stock."
IBM shares surged five to 122-1/4 in very active trade.

Earlier, Daniel Mandresh of Merrill Lynch upgraded his near-term rating on IBM to a strong buy from an accumulate, citing its recent mainframe and storage announcements as fueling strong earnings in the third and fourth quarters.
And SoundView Financial Group market strategist James Townsend said that technology stocks, the market laggards, are poised as a group to outperform the broad market once again.
Analysts said that the stock's minor technical breakout at 120 also may have added a little to the upside.
"It's a minor technical breakout," said Ricky Harrington, a technical analyst at Interstate/Johnson Lane.
"It may have been instrumental in adding a little bit of an upside to the stock," Harrington added. He said the next major resistance level for IBM is around 129.

IBM's shares indeed have been moribund this year and more so since this summer's technology stock meltdown. IBM trades at a very low price/earnings ratio for technology stocks, currently around 11 times 1996 earnings estimates.

But two weeks ago, IBM shares jumped 3-1/2 in one day to 115-1/4, after Salomon Brothers analyst John Jones raised his rating to a strong buy from a buy, with a 12-month price target of $145. Mandresh has a 12-month price target of $150.
